newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: IMF OFFICIAL SEEKS ARGENTINE TAX REFORM - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: IMF OFFICIAL SEEKS ARGENTINE TAX REFORM - PAPER.

text.p: Argentina should reform its taxation system to stop the current trend that allows people who earn a lot not to "pay what they should," a top International Monetary Fund (IMF) official was quoted Monday as saying.

"In Argentina people that earn a lot ... don't pay taxes on dividends. Don't pay taxes on banking (term deposits). They pay income tax. But this (tax) rate is not high," Vito Tanzi, head of the IMF's Fiscal Department told Clarin newspaper.
"The tax structure...must be corrected," he said.

"The current tax structure allowed many people to become rich...For example, people that made lots of capital, interest and dividend gains. These people are now rich and a decade ago they were not." To Clarin's assertion that many specialists say that taxing dividends and bank interest could scare investors away, Tanzi replied: "The negative impact of taxes on dividends and interest has been exaggerated."

Asked whether Argentina should apply a higher income tax rate, he answered: "Yes. Salaries ... are subject to social insurance tax, which is high. The 21 percent VAT burden is heavy. In all those cases the pressure is high."

"But reagrding income tax, I don't know why people complain ... In Italy income tax payments amount to 15 percent of GDP, while here it is only 2.5 percent ... In Chile the income tax is much higher than in Argentina. And Chile is a country that grows."

Asked whether the VAT rate could be trimmed, he said he would like a lower one but stressed that could only be achieved when public finances allowed. "So I think it should wait to see whether the tax evasion fight bears fruit. Or whether another tax is created to replace VAT."
